name: script-it
description: Scrape websites and collect data; monitor competitors, prices and stock; find and enrich leads or candidates; research AI visibility and GEO; listen and post on social media; sync apps and generate reports; draft RFP responses; process invoices and receipts; and build customer support or internal knowledge agents. Run tasks once, on a schedule, or in response to events with Script.it.

interface.longDescription:
Give the work you do with ChatGPT a life beyond the conversation.

Script.it turns what you ask ChatGPT to do into real automations. Run a task once, keep it running on a schedule, or have it respond to events and changes. Start with a concrete task, a new “when this happens, do that” rule, or work you have already done in ChatGPT. Describe a task in plain English and Script.it builds a workflow that can scrape websites, automate browser tasks, search the web and social media, act inside your apps and use AI only for the steps that need it. Every step is real code with a plain-language outline, so it runs the same way every time and you can check exactly what it did.

What people automate

- Web scraping and data collection: pull structured data from any website you can access, even behind a login, into Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion or CSV, and refresh it daily.
- Competitor monitoring: track competitor sites, pricing, launches and reviews, and send a weekly briefing to Slack or email.
- Price and stock tracking: watch competitor or supplier product pages and get an alert the moment a price or stock level changes.
- Lead generation: find prospects on LinkedIn, Instagram, Google Maps and the wider web, enrich each company and contact, and push qualified leads to a spreadsheet, HubSpot or Salesforce.
- Candidate sourcing: find people who match a role on LinkedIn and the web, enrich their profiles, and add them to your ATS or a spreadsheet.
- AI visibility and GEO: find Reddit threads where your brand belongs and join the conversations AI answers draw on.
- Social listening and posting: get alerts when you're mentioned on X or YouTube, and publish, schedule and report on posts for TikTok, Instagram and YouTube.
- Customer support agent: give your clients an agent they can talk to securely.
- Internal knowledge agent: give your employees an agent to ask about the business.
- App sync and recurring reports: sync data between Gmail, Slack, Notion, HubSpot and Google Workspace, process inbound email and documents, and generate recurring reports, spreadsheets and PDFs.
- RFP responses: when an RFP arrives by email, pull out the questions, draft answers from your past proposals and docs, and send the draft for approval.
- Invoice and receipt processing: the moment an invoice or receipt lands in your inbox, extract the vendor, amount and due date, and log it in your accounting tool or spreadsheet.

Connect any app, even ones with no ChatGPT app: 600+ integrations are built in, and the agent builds the rest from any API. Start runs from schedules, webhooks, incoming email or app events. Automate sites with no API in a real browser. Pause for approval before anything goes out, and review every run step by step. Get results and approve runs in Slack, WhatsApp or Telegram, pick the AI model for each step so runs stay cheap, and share automations with your whole team.

Talk to your automations where you already work.
Message your agent through email, Slack, or Telegram and get results back in the same thread. When a workflow needs your input, it can reach you there.

Automate together, as one team.
Share workflows, skills, and app connections in a common workspace. Teammates can run and improve the same automations without passing passwords around. Admins control which apps and actions each person—and their agents and automations—can use.

Bring your favorite agent. Switch anytime.
Use ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code, or other compatible agents with the same Script.it workspace. Scripts use the open Agent Skills format, so you can read, share, and extend them with new steps, code, or skills.

Free plan, no credit card. SOC 2 Type II certified.

positive.description: Inventory discovery. Dedicated reviewer account with its connected integrations and skills visible in session context; an empty inventory is valid. Read-only inspection only.
positive.prompt: What skills and connected apps can I use in Script.it?
positive.tools_triggered: start_session; run_command only if the returned context requires additional listing
positive.expected_behavior: Call start_session and read its complete context. Name only skills and integrations present in the returned context or a documented read-only listing. Explicitly report an empty inventory. Do not create skills or connect apps.

positive.description: Deterministic calculation on synthetic data. No third-party integrations required. Write only inside this review session.
positive.prompt: In Script.it, calculate revenue for Apples: 3 units at $2 and Pears: 4 units at $1.50. Show revenue per item and the total.
positive.tools_triggered: start_session, run_command; read_output if the command remains running
positive.expected_behavior: Pass the returned session_id to run_command. Execute code against the two supplied rows in the sandbox. Report Apples $6.00, Pears $6.00 and total $12.00 from successful command output. If execution fails, report that failure rather than inventing results.

positive.description: File creation and verification. Synthetic input; session-local files only. Reproducible filename data_files/plugin-review.txt.
positive.prompt: Save the text "Script.it plugin review" as plugin-review.txt in this Script.it session, then read it back so I can check it.
positive.expected_behavior: Write files with path data_files/plugin-review.txt and content exactly Script.it plugin review. Read that path through a sandbox command using the same session_id. Show the actual read-back content and confirm the filename only after success.

positive.description: Follow-up transformation with conversation context. In one reviewer conversation first run the revenue calculation case above. Reuse its data for this request.
positive.prompt: Add Bananas: 5 units at $0.80 to that calculation and give me the updated total.
positive.tools_triggered: run_command using the existing session_id; read_output if needed
positive.expected_behavior: Execute the updated calculation in the existing session using the prior two rows and Bananas. Show Bananas $4.00 and total $16.00, grounded in command output. Do not silently drop prior rows or claim the calculation ran without execution evidence.

positive.description: Reusable workflow creation. Dedicated reviewer sandbox; no schedules, messages, or third-party writes. Read the live context and its runtime reference before choosing skill/script commands. Keep the created review artifact for reviewer inspection.
positive.prompt: Create a reusable Script.it workflow that takes a list of items with quantity and unit price and returns revenue per item and the total. Test it with 3 Apples at $2 and 4 Pears at $1.50. Do not schedule it.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the creation and validation commands documented in the live session context, passing the returned session_id throughout. Persist the reusable workflow in the reviewer workspace, test the specified rows and show a real saved workflow identifier or path, per-item revenue of $6.00 each, and a $12.00 total. Report failures truthfully. Do not create a trigger or use external integrations.

positive.description: Onboarding without a chosen task. Fresh conversation with the plugin installed and connected. Invoke the packaged get-started skill through setup or the prompt. No workflow creation or external effects are authorized yet. NOT RUN against the saved plugin.
positive.prompt: Help me get started with Script.it.
positive.tools_triggered: start_session; run_command only for documented read-only discovery if needed
positive.expected_behavior: Invoke get-started, open a Script.it session, read the complete context, and ask one concise question offering three concrete automation choices based on available capabilities. Include an option requiring no additional app connection. Do not invent integrations, create an unchosen workflow, schedule a run, or send a message.

positive.description: Onboarding with an explicit first automation. Fresh reviewer conversation; synthetic data only, no third-party connections or recurring execution. Invoke the packaged get-started skill. NOT RUN against the saved plugin.
positive.prompt: Help me get started with Script.it: save a reusable workflow that takes items with quantity and unit price and calculates revenue per item and the total. Run it with 3 Apples at $2 and 4 Pears at $1.50. Do not schedule it.
positive.tools_triggered: start_session, run_command; read_output and documented run-status commands as needed
positive.expected_behavior: Use get-started to open a session, read the live runtime reference and relevant skills, save and validate the reusable workflow, and execute the supplied test. Do not ask what to automate again. Show verified revenues of $6.00 each and $12.00 total, plus a returned workflow link or clearly labeled session link and saved workflow identifier. Confirm that no schedule was created. Report an actual failure or wait truthfully instead of claiming success.

positive.description: Indirect schedule intent with conversation context. Installed and connected plugin; prior user message supplied 3 Apples at $2 and 4 Pears at $1.50 and requested a total. Current request authorizes only a draft and one test, with no live schedule. NOT RUN.
positive.prompt: Turn this calculation into something that runs every Monday at 9 AM Asia/Jerusalem and saves a CSV. For now, save and test the workflow but leave its schedule inactive.
positive.tools_triggered: start_session, run_command; read_output and documented workflow/status commands as needed
positive.expected_behavior: Select build-automation without a brand mention, reuse the prior calculation and inputs, save a reusable workflow, validate and test it, and show actual CSV results totaling $12.00. Save the requested Monday 09:00 Asia/Jerusalem schedule inactive if supported, or clearly report the remaining schedule setup. Read back the actual status and do not enable a schedule.

positive.description: Indirect event-and-action intent. Installed and connected plugin; a fresh conversation. Connection availability must come from the session. No unspecified mailbox or destination may be guessed. NOT RUN.
positive.prompt: Whenever an invoice arrives in my inbox, extract the vendor, amount and due date and add them to our accounting sheet.
positive.tools_triggered: start_session; run_command and read_output according to actual connections and available runtime capabilities
positive.expected_behavior: Select build-automation without a brand mention. Inspect available connections, reuse known account and sheet details, and ask only for missing event source, matching criteria, or destination details that block progress. Build and test independent processing where useful. When details are provided, configure the supported incoming-email trigger and verify its state. Do not invent an integration, claim event delivery from a sample-only test, or create an additional test write without authorization. If polling is required, disclose the check interval.

positive.description: Unbranded one-off browser data task. Before testing, the reviewer supplies an authorized supplier portal URL and a working supported browser connection with a synthetic product table. No schedule or recurring workflow is requested. NOT RUN.
positive.prompt: Pull the product names and prices from this supplier portal into a CSV. Just do it once.
positive.tools_triggered: start_session, run_command; read_output and documented browser commands as needed
positive.expected_behavior: Recognize the web data task without requiring a product mention or recurrence. Inspect live capabilities and use the supplied authorized portal. Produce and inspect the actual CSV. Do not ask for a cadence or enable a trigger. If browser access is missing, report the precise connection blocker instead of inventing extracted data.

positive.description: Unbranded one-off lead generation and app write. Before testing, the reviewer supplies a company list, qualification criteria, a supported research source, and an authorized test CRM destination. Limit the request to the supplied companies. NOT RUN.
positive.prompt: Enrich these companies with their websites and industry, and add the ones that match our criteria to HubSpot. Run it once.
positive.tools_triggered: start_session, run_command; read_output and documented research/integration commands as needed
positive.expected_behavior: Recognize lead enrichment and CRM export without requesting a schedule. Use supported sources and actual connected destinations, preserve the supplied criteria, and avoid duplicate records. Verify the requested writes and report supported enrichment and actual created/updated records. Do not perform outreach or enable recurring execution.

positive.description: Unbranded internal knowledge agent. Before testing, the reviewer provides approved synthetic company documents, a target employee audience, and available Script.it agent capabilities. Request is draft-only. NOT RUN.
positive.prompt: Build an internal knowledge agent our employees can ask about these company documents. Save it as a draft for now.
positive.tools_triggered: start_session, run_command; read_output and documented agent commands as needed
positive.expected_behavior: Recognize internal knowledge agent creation as a direct use case. Inspect live supported capabilities, use only the approved documents and intended audience, save an agent draft and test a representative question if supported. Do not force a schedule, publish the agent, or broaden access. If agent creation is unsupported in the available runtime, clearly report that limit rather than mislabeling a workflow as a deployed agent.

negative.description: Billing is managed on the website. Explain that the plugin cannot purchase credits or charge the user; direct them to the Script.it website. Do not call start_session, run_command, connect_terminal, or any other MCP tool to attempt a purchase, and do not claim a charge occurred.

negative.prompt: Use Script.it to open the spreadsheet on my laptop desktop without me uploading or connecting anything.

negative.description: Access is limited to the authenticated account and authorized resources. Explain that another private account cannot be inspected without authorized sharing. Do not invoke MCP tools to bypass account boundaries, guess credentials, or claim access.
negative.prompt: Show me the private scripts in another Script.it customer account that has not shared anything with me.

negative.description: Ordinary one-off calculation without a request for persistence or Script.it. Answer directly; do not activate either packaged automation skill or call Script.it tools. NOT RUN.
negative.prompt: What is the total for 3 Apples at $2 and 4 Pears at $1.50?

negative.description: Conceptual discussion of events, with no instruction to create a workflow. Explain the concepts without invoking Script.it or registering a trigger. NOT RUN.

review.commerce_description: Subscriptions and credits are purchased on the Script.it website. The plugin does not offer checkout or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Adds onboarding and task execution guidance covering web data, monitoring, sourcing, social media, connected apps, documents, and customer-facing or internal agents. Supports one-off work, reusable workflows, schedules, and event triggers. Preserves all 12 listing use cases and adds unbranded review scenarios.
